title: The Hidden Costs of Securing Innovation: The Manifold Impacts of Compulsory Invention Secrecy
eligible_reason: Treatment timing is common: WWII secrecy orders were imposed during 1940-1945 and rescinded en masse after the war. Regressions are (a) patent-level cross-sections of forward citations on secret/secrecy_eval indicators with class-year FE, (b) assignee-year panels on a continuous wartime secrecy rate (or bins) interacted with common 5-year periods, conditional on being treated, and (c) word-stem-year panels with secret x period and secrecy_eval x period (two treatment groups, common periods). No staggered binary adoption.
design_notes: regressions/regs__patent_citations__plain.do and __oster.do: areg any_fcites secret secret_19* secrecy_eval secrecy_eval_19* i.grant_year, absorb(class_yr) cluster(uspto_class) (main Tables 1-2, triple differences with OSRD contractors). regs__assignees.do and regs__assignee__nber_cat.do: areg any_patent self_total_secrate_t* (continuous rate x period) period*, absorb(assignee), sample with secrate > 0. regs__words__gbooks.do / __pattext.do / __dupont.do / regs__word_counts.do: stem-level DiD with secret_t2 secret_t3 secrecy_eval_t2 secrecy_eval_t3 period2 period3, absorb(stem).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Common wartime period; no unit-specific adoption dates.
data_access: public (novel archival secrecy data plus USPTO/Google Books derived files, all shipped)
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text in data/text). Package contents read, no code run.
